description: Complete beat type definitions for ASAPS Modern with nested connection architecture, cluster container support, and schema-driven normalize/validate metadata (conditionTypes registry, parameter aliases, primitive coercion)

connectionModel.description: Defines how connections are structured within beats
principles: Connections are semantically part of the function's behavior
Single-connection beats have connection within function
Multi-connection beats have choices/props that contain targets
All connections support labels, conditions, and effects

dialogNode.description: A node in a dialog tree representing NPC/system output. Followed by player choices, or auto-advances if target is set with no choices.
dialogNode.notes: dialogNode displays text. If 'target' is set and no visible choices exist, auto-advances to the target beat after a delay (NPC exit). Otherwise waits for player to click a choice.

dialogChoice.description: A player choice in dialog. Can exit to a beat or continue with nested dialog.
dialogChoice.notes: Either 'target' (beat ID to exit) OR 'dialogNode' (continue conversation), not both. Counter fields allow direct counter modification (any counter name) in addition to effects[]. soundEffect plays when this choice is selected. P3-3c-9 — optional `hotspot` (normalized 0–1 against the spatial image) flips the CURRENT dialog node into spatial mode: the renderer composes speaker/text into flow slots over the beat background and turns the choices into clickable regions on the image. Per-node, so a dialogTree can mix spatial nodes (a scene) with positioned nodes (a close-up monologue).

multiChoiceOption.description: A button-style choice in a MultiChoice beat (NPC text + several response buttons, single level, no spatial layer). Same per-choice effect surface as a movementOption / dialogChoice, but no location / hotspot fields — the choice is always a button.
multiChoiceOption.notes: displayText is the translated/display label; text is the internal identifier. soundEffect plays when this choice is selected. Effects apply per-choice (variable/counter/inventory/affect/etc.) — same surface as DialogTree's dialogChoice and MovementChoice's movementOption.

movementOption.notes: Counter fields allow direct counter modification (any counter name) in addition to effects[]. soundEffect plays when this choice is selected. locationName optionally references a hotspot or prop from beat.locations by name. displayText is the translated/display label; text is the internal identifier used for hotspot matching. P3-3c — optional `hotspot` carries a normalized 0–1 rectangle on the spatial layer; when ALL choices have hotspots AND the beat has no baked locations, the renderer composes movementChoice through SpatialFlowView with the image as background and the hotspots as clickable regions.

propOption.notes: If assetId is provided, prop is rendered as clickable graphic from assets. Otherwise rendered as button. Counter fields allow direct counter modification. soundEffect plays when this prop is selected. locationName optionally references a hotspot or prop from beat.locations by name for Visual Editor association. inventoryName overrides the item name added to inventory (defaults to locationName or name). displayName overrides the label shown on hotspots (defaults to name). Useful for translations where name must stay as internal key.

effect.description: Effect to apply to story state

connection.description: Single connection for linear beats

spatialHotspot.description: Normalized 0–1 clickable region on the spatial image (P3-3c). Coordinates are RELATIVE to the LETTERBOXED image rect (objectFit:'contain'), so the hotspot tracks the picture pixels across viewports / orientations.

panoramaHotspot.description: A hotspot in a 360° panorama placed at pitch/yaw coordinates
panoramaHotspot.notes: pitch is vertical angle (-90 to 90), yaw is horizontal angle (-180 to 180). target is the beat ID to navigate to when clicked. locationName optionally references a hotspot, prop, or character from beat.locations by name. soundEffect plays when this hotspot is selected.

_meta.description: Per-condition-type field requirements. Drives the schema-driven normalize/validate pipeline (v0.9.51+). Each entry lists the condition's discriminator value, its required fields, and optional fields. The 'type' field itself is always required as the discriminator. The pipeline uses this to: (1) flatten condition.* into top-level params via the conditionBeat 'nested' block, (2) validate that the required fields for the chosen type are present, (3) emit warnings for unknown fields. Replaces the hardcoded per-condition-type required-field map in AIValidator.ts and the partial flattening passes in AIService and App.tsx.

variable.description: Compare a story variable against a value. AI commonly emits `variable` or `left`; pipeline aliases either to `variableName`.

counter.description: Compare a counter against a value (variableName is the counter name). AI commonly emits `variable`, `left`, or `counter` — pipeline aliases all to `variableName`.

counterCompare.description: Compare two counters against each other

timer.description: Compare a timer's remaining seconds against a value

inventory.description: Check whether a character holds an item (character defaults to 'player'; checkType: has | notHas | quantity)

visitedBeat.description: Branch on whether a named beat has been visited

fictionalTime.description: Compare the story's fictional time against a target time

mood.description: Compare a character's mood (valence or arousal axis) against a value. baseline: 'literal' | 'initial' | { bookmark: name }

emotion.description: Compare a character's emotion intensity against a value

sentiment.description: Compare a character's sentiment toward a target against a value. sentimentEmotion optional — empty sums all emotions toward target

trait.description: Compare a character's static trait value against a value

goal.description: Branch on a character's goal status (open | met | failed | abandoned). Status read from goalStatus or value.

characterVariant.description: Branch on which variant is currently active on a character. variantId or value carries the compared variant id.

gpsProximity.description: Branch on player's distance to a GPS target. proximityMode: 'within' | 'outside'.

indoorProximity.description: Branch on a Bluetooth beacon's signal strength. proximityMode: 'within' | 'outside'.

permissionGranted.description: Branch on whether the player has granted a sensor permission (location | beacons | …)

slotIntent.description: Soft responsive layout intent for slot-mode rendering (per-slot preferredLines / anchor / gap). Visual-Editor managed; NEVER serialized as baked locations[] — a beat carrying slotIntent and no locations[] stays responsive (slot mode). Absent → pure flow.

slotAnimations.description: Responsive motion intent for slot-mode rendering (P3-anim). Per-slot enter/exit/emphasis presets resolved against the slot's responsive box — survives reflow/orientation. Distinct from the legacy `animations` (AnimationPath[] over absolute x/y). Absent → no animation. P3-anim-1 supports the 'fade' enter preset; further presets land per the P3-anim phasing in project_responsive_layout_system memory.

spatialAnimations.description: Responsive motion intent for the SPATIAL layer (Phase-3 composite image). Cinematic enter presets — ken-burns, zoom-in, zoom-out, pan-{left,right,up,down}. Resolved against the image's currently-rendered rect, so motion survives reflow / viewport. Distinct from slotAnimations (flow layer). Absent → no animation. Only meaningful for spatial-mode beats.

spatialFit.description: How the background image fits the stage. 'contain' (default) preserves the full image with letterboxed bars when aspect ratios differ; 'cover' fills the stage and may crop the image's edges. Override the schema-level default per beat.

dialogTree.layoutModeNote: P3-3c-9 — dialogTree flips into spatial mode PER NODE: a node whose choices each carry a `hotspot` composes through SpatialFlowView (image as background, speaker/text in flow slots, choices as clickable regions on the image). Positioned-presentation only — chat-scroll / chat-bubble keep their own renderers. Authors can mix spatial nodes (scenes) with positioned nodes (close-up monologues) within a single dialogTree.

aiNotes.structure: dialogTree alternates: dialogNode (NPC speaks) → choices (player clicks - text IS player's dialogue) → dialogNode (NPC responds) → choices...
aiNotes.pattern: Each dialogNode has speaker, text, and choices array. Player must click a choice to continue.
aiNotes.choiceNavigation: Each choice has text (player's line) and EITHER 'target' (beat ID to exit) OR 'dialogNode' (NPC responds), never both
aiNotes.critical: Choice text IS the player's dialogue. NEVER use '[Continue]' or placeholder text. Every choice should be meaningful player dialogue.
aiNotes.effects: Use effects on choices to modify counters or variables when player selects that choice
aiNotes.example: { id: 'root', speaker: 'NPC', text: 'Hello!', choices: [{ id: 'c1', text: 'Hi there!', dialogNode: { id: 'n1', speaker: 'NPC', text: 'Nice day!', choices: [{ id: 'c2', text: 'Indeed it is. Goodbye!', target: 'next_beat' }] } }] }

'custom' reads slotIntent anchors for fine-grained author control. setVariable.description: Modify story variables or counters (or fictional-time clock)

type.description: Discriminator: 'variable' | 'counter' | 'fictionalTime'. Drives which fields below are read at runtime.

name.description: Variable or counter name (ignored when type='fictionalTime' — the runtime targets the project's fictional-time clock instead)

character.description: type='counter' only. Counter owner. OMIT for a story-global counter (default — world/plot tallies). Set to a Character id/name to scope the counter to that character's per-character store (per-character stats like health/trust). Unlike inventory there is no implicit 'player' default — absence means global. Ignored for type='variable'|'fictionalTime'.

value.description: New value (string for variables, number for counters). Prefix with '=' (spreadsheet convention) to compute an arithmetic expression at runtime, e.g. "= (var1 + var2) / 100" — supports + - * / parentheses, unary minus, numeric literals, and variable/counter references (plain identifiers like score, plus ${name}, $name$, {name}; names resolve against variables first, then counters; character-scoped counters via owner.counter, e.g. alice.trust). If evaluation fails (unknown reference, division by zero, syntax error) the raw string is stored unchanged. Without the leading '=' nothing is evaluated — '5+3' stays the literal string '5+3'. For type='fictionalTime' with operation='advance'/'subtract', this is the magnitude (paired with timeUnit). Empty/zero is a valid value.

connection.description: Next beat after variable/counter is set

timeUnit.description: type='fictionalTime' / operation='advance'|'subtract' only. Unit of advance: 'minutes' | 'hours' | 'days' | 'weeks' | 'months' | 'years'.

setGpsLocation.description: Write a named GPS point set into story state — capture the player's current position, set explicit coordinates, or randomly scatter points around a center. A GpsLocation beat can then geofence the named set dynamically (bind an entry to the same name), and a Condition beat can react to it.

mode.description: 'capture' pins the player's current position; 'explicit' stores author-entered coordinates; 'scatter' randomly distributes points within a radius of a center at play time; 'preset' writes a set of points you place and review on a map at authoring time (optionally auto-generated onto streets/parks).

presetPoints.description: preset mode: author-curated GPS points ({ lat, lng, radiusMeters? }) placed and reviewed on a map, optionally auto-generated onto walkable streets/parks. Written verbatim at play time — no network or sensor needed.

pointName.description: Name of the GPS point set to write. Reference this name from a GpsLocation entry (its 'pointName') to geofence these points.

lat.description: Latitude (WGS84). Used by 'explicit' mode, and by 'scatter' when the center source is explicit coordinates.

lng.description: Longitude (WGS84). Used by 'explicit' mode, and by 'scatter' when the center source is explicit coordinates.

pointRadiusMeters.description: Optional geofence radius (metres) stamped on each stored point; falls back to the GpsLocation beat's radius when omitted.

count.description: scatter mode: how many points to generate.

scatterRadiusMeters.description: scatter mode: maximum distance (metres) from the center to scatter points.

centerSource.description: scatter mode: where the scatter is centered.

centerPointName.description: scatter mode with center source 'point': the name of the point set to center on (uses its first point).

placement.description: scatter mode: 'uniform' places points by pure math (offline, may land inside buildings/water); 'walkable' snaps points onto real streets, paths, and parks via OpenStreetMap (needs a network connection at play time; falls back to uniform when coverage is thin or the lookup fails).

fallbackLat.description: Fallback latitude used when the sensor is unavailable / permission denied (capture, or scatter-from-current).

fallbackLng.description: Fallback longitude used when the sensor is unavailable / permission denied (capture, or scatter-from-current).

connection.description: Next beat after the points are stored

condition.description: AI emits the condition as a nested object. Pipeline flattens its fields to top-level params (using the conditionTypes registry to know which fields are valid for the chosen type), then deletes the nested object. After flatten, conditionType is the top-level discriminator.

The runtime accepts both forms; the schema declares string because it's the most general (variable refs need to be strings). updateAffect.description: Nudge a character's mood and/or strengthen a sentiment toward another entity. The runtime clamps each axis and sentiment strength to [-1, 1].

moodValenceDelta.description: Pushes the character's mood pleasanter (positive) or unpleasanter (negative). Runtime clamps the resulting mood to [-1, 1].

moodArousalDelta.description: Pushes the character calmer (negative) or more excited (positive). Clamped to [-1, 1].

sentimentTarget.description: Entity the sentiment is directed at (Character.id, item name, beat id, or any author tag).

sentimentEmotion.description: Emotion label (e.g. trust, fear, anger, joy, pride, shame). Free-text — no enforced palette.

sentimentDelta.description: Adds to (or subtracts from) the existing (target, emotion) sentiment strength. Negative values weaken or invert the feeling. Clamped to [-1, 1].

emotion.description: Emotion name to fire (e.g. joy, anger, fear). When the emotion is in the project's emotion palette, mood is auto-nudged by its weights — no need to also set mood deltas above. Unknown names still update the level but skip the mood side-effect so typos are surfaced.

emotionDelta.description: Intensity delta for the named emotion. Positive bumps the emotion; negative reduces it. Clamped to [0, 1] post-add.

connection.description: Next beat after the affect update

effects.description: v0.9.45+ canonical shape — an ordered list of Effects (mood nudge, sentiment delta, emotion fire, goal status, variant switch, bookmark, …). When present, this replaces the legacy single-row fields above (moodValenceDelta, sentimentTarget, …). The migration helpers in core promote legacy shapes into this array on load.

gpsLocation.description: Show one or more GPS-anchored locations on a map. Each location has its own next-beat target and Effects bundle (counters, mood, sentiment, etc) — the first location the player crosses into (or out of) wins, like a movement choice on a map. The runtime probes GPS permission via ensureXRPermission and falls back per the project's LocationSettings.onPermissionDenied policy.

mode.description: Behaviour mode: 'display' shows the map with a continue button (no waiting); 'trigger-on-arrival' resolves when the player enters the radius; 'trigger-on-departure' resolves when the player leaves it.

targetLat.description: Target latitude in degrees (WGS84). E.g. 51.5074 for London.

targetLng.description: Target longitude in degrees (WGS84). E.g. -0.1278 for London.

radiusMeters.description: Proximity radius in metres. Falls back to the project's LocationSettings.defaultProximityRadiusM when unset, then 25m.

text.description: Instructional text shown over the map (e.g. 'Walk to the meeting point at the fountain').

cancelButtonText.description: Optional skip / cancel button label. Lets the player exit the beat without waiting for arrival.

timeoutMs.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds. The beat resolves with 'timeout' if no arrival / departure / skip happens within this window.

showPlayerMarker.description: Whether to show the player's current location on the map.

connection.description: Next beat after the GPS beat resolves (regardless of how — arrival, timeout, skip).

indoorLocation.description: Show a floor plan for this beat with one or more target Bluetooth beacons. Each beat carries its own floor plan + dimensions, so different beats can show different rooms or scales. Each location has its own (x, y) on this floor plan, beaconUuid, target beat, and Effects bundle. The first beacon the player walks within radius wins.

mode.description: Behaviour mode: 'display' shows the floor plan with a continue button; 'trigger-on-arrival' resolves when the player enters the radius around the target beacon; 'trigger-on-departure' resolves when the player leaves it.

targetBeaconUuid.description: UUID of the target beacon — must match a beacon configured in Project Settings → Location & XR → Indoor venue → Beacons.

radiusMeters.description: Proximity radius in metres. Falls back to LocationSettings.defaultProximityRadiusM when unset, then 5m (room-scale default — indoor is tighter than outdoor).

text.description: Instructional text shown over the floor plan (e.g. 'Find the artefact in the east wing').

timeoutMs.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds. Beat resolves with 'timeout' if no arrival / departure / skip within this window.

connection.description: Next beat after the indoor-location beat resolves.

qrScan.description: Opens the camera and waits for the player to scan a QR code. The decoded string is saved to a variable, then the beat branches.

prompt.description: Instruction shown above the camera preview

matchPatterns.description: Optional regex patterns — only codes that match resolve. Leave empty to accept any code.

qrJumpTargets.description: Authoring metadata only: beat IDs that printed asaps://beat/<id> QR codes for this beat jump to. arBeat.description: Augmented-reality scene with marker tracking. The player aims the camera at a printed marker; overlay anchors (text, image, tappable cards) attach to the marker. Each anchor's tap routes through an asaps:// URI or target beat id, so authors get treasure-hunt / pick-the-clue mechanics without scripting.

prompt.description: Instruction shown above the AR view

trackingMode.description: How anchors are placed in the scene. Phase 1: only 'marker' is implemented (image-target tracking via MindAR). 'world' and 'face' are reserved for Phase 2.

markerAssetId.description: Asset ID of a pre-compiled .mind file produced by the MindAR compiler (https://hiukim.github.io/mind-ar-js-doc/tools/compile/). Used as the image target the camera tracks.

anchors.description: Overlay anchors attached to the marker. Each anchor has a label, optional sprite, and an onTap target (asaps:// URI or beat id).

label.description: Text shown on the anchor card / tooltip

assetId.description: Optional image asset shown as a billboard at the anchor position

anchoredTo.description: marker:<id> = pinned to a tracked marker; world:tap = appears where the player taps (Phase 2)

offsetX.description: Local-space X offset from the marker center (-1..1)

offsetY.description: Local-space Y offset from the marker center (-1..1)

onTap.description: asaps:// URI (e.g. asaps://beat/<id>) OR a bare target beat id to jump to when the anchor is tapped
